claims.title: Turkana Boy lives near Lake Turkana
claims.summary: A Homo erectus youth, later catalogued KNM-WT 15000, lives near what is now the Nariokotome River; his fossilised skeleton would become the most complete of its species ever recovered.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1600000bce-turkana-boy-lives-near-lake-turkana, claim TL:KEN:event:1600000bce:turkana-boy-lives-near-lake-turkana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hominins at Koobi Fora
claims.summary: The Koobi Fora deposits east of Lake Turkana preserve fossils of Paranthropus boisei and early Homo, making the area one of the world's leading sites for the study of human evolution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1900000bce-hominins-at-koobi-fora, claim TL:KEN:event:1900000bce:hominins-at-koobi-fora, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cushitic pastoralists enter the north
claims.summary: Southern Cushitic-speaking herders move into the arid lands of northern Kenya, among the earliest food-producing communities in the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-3000bce-cushitic-pastoralists-enter-the-north, claim TL:KEN:event:3000bce:cushitic-pastoralists-enter-the-north, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Olorgesailie tool traditions and the Stone Age
claims.summary: Sites such as Olorgesailie in the Rift Valley preserve vast accumulations of hand-axes and other tools, documenting hundreds of thousands of years of Stone Age life in Kenya.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1000bce-olorgesailie-tool-traditions-and-the-stone-age, claim TL:KEN:event:1000bce:olorgesailie-tool-traditions-and-the-stone-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bantu expansion reaches western Kenya
claims.summary: Iron-using Bantu-speaking farmers spread into western Kenya, part of the wider Bantu expansion that reshaped much of eastern and southern Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1000bce-bantu-expansion-reaches-western-kenya, claim TL:KEN:event:1000bce:bantu-expansion-reaches-western-kenya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Swahili coast
claims.summary: Coastal Bantu communities trading across the Indian Ocean develop the Swahili language and an Afro-Islamic urban culture, founding settlements that grow into city-states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-800-rise-of-the-swahili-coast, claim TL:KEN:event:800:rise-of-the-swahili-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ibn Battuta visits Mombasa
claims.summary: The traveller Ibn Battuta describes Mombasa and Kilwa as prosperous, pious Muslim trading towns, attesting to the wealth of the medieval Swahili coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1331-ibn-battuta-visits-mombasa, claim TL:KEN:event:1331:ibn-battuta-visits-mombasa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zheng He's fleet reaches Malindi
claims.summary: Vessels of the Chinese admiral Zheng He's treasure fleet are recorded reaching Malindi, marking the eastern extent of the Indian Ocean trade that linked the Swahili coast to China.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1418-zheng-he-s-fleet-reaches-malindi, claim TL:KEN:event:1418:zheng-he-s-fleet-reaches-malindi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Southern Luo migrate into western Kenya
claims.summary: Nilotic-speaking Luo communities move into the Lake Victoria basin of western Kenya, the last major wave of the migrations that formed the country's peoples.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1450-southern-luo-migrate-into-western-kenya, claim TL:KEN:event:1450:southern-luo-migrate-into-western-kenya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vasco da Gama reaches the Kenyan coast
claims.summary: The Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama calls at Mombasa and Malindi en route to India, beginning a century of Portuguese involvement on the Swahili coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1498-vasco-da-gama-reaches-the-kenyan-coast, claim TL:KEN:event:1498:vasco-da-gama-reaches-the-kenyan-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese build Fort Jesus
claims.summary: The Portuguese construct Fort Jesus at Mombasa to a Renaissance design by Giovanni Battista Cairati, anchoring their control of the coast and the Indian Ocean trade routes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1593-portuguese-build-fort-jesus, claim TL:KEN:event:1593:portuguese-build-fort-jesus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Omani Arabs capture Fort Jesus
claims.summary: After a siege of some thirty-three months, Omani forces take Fort Jesus, ending Portuguese dominance and bringing the Kenyan coast, Zanzibar and Pemba under Omani Arab control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1698-omani-arabs-capture-fort-jesus, claim TL:KEN:event:1698:omani-arabs-capture-fort-jesus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zanzibar becomes the Omani capital
claims.summary: Sultan Seyyid Said moves the Omani capital from Muscat to Zanzibar, making the island the centre of a commercial empire to which the Kenyan coast was bound.

sources.label: Muscat — Architectural Heritage
sources.publisher: The National Museum, Sultanate of Oman

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1840-zanzibar-becomes-the-omani-capital, claim TL:KEN:event:1840:zanzibar-becomes-the-omani-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fort Jesus inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: Fort Jesus is added to the UNESCO World Heritage List as an outstanding example of sixteenth-century military architecture and a witness to the contest for the Indian Ocean trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-2011-fort-jesus-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:KEN:event:2011:fort-jesus-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: East Africa Protectorate established
claims.summary: Britain proclaims the East Africa Protectorate over the territory that would become Kenya, beginning nearly seven decades of formal British rule.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Kenya / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1895-east-africa-protectorate-established, claim TL:KEN:event:1895:east-africa-protectorate-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Uganda Railway is built
claims.summary: The 'Lunatic Line' is driven from Mombasa to Lake Victoria, built largely by indentured Indian labourers; it reaches Nairobi in 1899 and opens the interior to settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1896-the-uganda-railway-is-built, claim TL:KEN:event:1896:the-uganda-railway-is-built, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kenya Colony created
claims.summary: The protectorate's interior becomes the Crown colony of Kenya, while a coastal strip leased from the sultan of Zanzibar remains a protectorate.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Kenya / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1920-kenya-colony-created, claim TL:KEN:event:1920:kenya-colony-created, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Harry Thuku founds early protest
claims.summary: Harry Thuku establishes the Young Kikuyu Association, one of the first organised African political movements against colonial land and labour policies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1921-harry-thuku-founds-early-protest, claim TL:KEN:event:1921:harry-thuku-founds-early-protest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kenyatta leads the Kenya African Union
claims.summary: Jomo Kenyatta, back from years in Britain, becomes president of the Kenya African Union, the leading vehicle of African nationalist demands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1947-kenyatta-leads-the-kenya-african-union, claim TL:KEN:event:1947:kenyatta-leads-the-kenya-african-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: State of emergency declared
claims.summary: As the Mau Mau revolt spreads, the colonial government declares a state of emergency that lasts until 1960, ushering in mass detentions and a brutal counter-insurgency.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1952-state-of-emergency-declared, claim TL:KEN:event:1952:state-of-emergency-declared, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jomo Kenyatta convicted
claims.summary: Kenyatta is tried and imprisoned for allegedly directing the Mau Mau, in proceedings later widely denounced as a sham; he is freed in 1961.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1953-jomo-kenyatta-convicted, claim TL:KEN:event:1953:jomo-kenyatta-convicted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lancaster House conferences
claims.summary: Three constitutional conferences in London negotiate Kenya's path to independence amid rivalry between KANU and the federalist KADU.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1960-lancaster-house-conferences, claim TL:KEN:event:1960:lancaster-house-conferences, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Internal self-government (Madaraka)
claims.summary: Kenya attains internal self-government under a KANU government led by Kenyatta, six months before full independence.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Kenya / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1963-internal-self-government-madaraka, claim TL:KEN:event:1963:internal-self-government-madaraka, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kenya becomes independent
claims.summary: Kenya gains independence from the United Kingdom with Jomo Kenyatta as prime minister; one year later, on 12 December 1964, it becomes a republic.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Kenya / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1963-kenya-becomes-independent, claim TL:KEN:event:1963:kenya-becomes-independent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Moi succeeds Kenyatta
claims.summary: On Kenyatta's death, Vice-President Daniel arap Moi becomes president, beginning a 24-year tenure that formalises the one-party state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1978-moi-succeeds-kenyatta, claim TL:KEN:event:1978:moi-succeeds-kenyatta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Failed coup attempt
claims.summary: Air-force officers attempt to overthrow Moi; the coup is crushed and followed by tighter political control and a constitutionally entrenched one-party state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1982-failed-coup-attempt, claim TL:KEN:event:1982:failed-coup-attempt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to multiparty politics
claims.summary: Under domestic and international pressure, Kenya amends its constitution to legalise opposition parties, paving the way for the multiparty elections of 1992.

sources.label: U.S. Relations With Kenya / History
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-1991-return-to-multiparty-politics, claim TL:KEN:event:1991:return-to-multiparty-politics, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kibaki ends KANU rule
claims.summary: Mwai Kibaki wins the presidency, ending nearly four decades of unbroken KANU government since independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-2002-kibaki-ends-kanu-rule, claim TL:KEN:event:2002:kibaki-ends-kanu-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Post-election violence
claims.summary: Kibaki's disputed re-election sparks ethnic and political violence that kills more than 1,100 people; a power-sharing deal brokered by Kofi Annan is signed on 28 February 2008.

sources.label: Turning Pebbles: Post-Election Violence in Kenya

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-2007-post-election-violence, claim TL:KEN:event:2007:post-election-violence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: New constitution adopted
claims.summary: Kenyans approve a new constitution that limits presidential power, expands rights, and devolves authority to 47 county governments.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kenya: From the cradle of humankind on Lake Turkana to the Swahili coast and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/KEN/chronicle#ev-2010-new-constitution-adopted, claim TL:KEN:event:2010:new-constitution-adopted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
